name: Abidul Qohar
headline: Embedded engineer, on the road to
bio: I'm Abidul Qohar, an embedded electronics engineer from Surabaya, now doing my master's in Yogyakarta. This page is my own corner of the internet — my past, my present, and my future, with the photos, projects, and work that come with them.
heroCaption: Me, at the museum — Yogyakarta days
heroAlt: Abidul giving a thumbs up in front of a museum display of traditional masks

ppf.label: Past
ppf.title: Where I started
ppf.text: Racing planes at PENS, IoT freelance work, teaching robotics, and engineering jobs across Surabaya — the years that made me an embedded engineer.

ppf.label: Present
ppf.title: Where I am now
ppf.text: Master's studies at UGM, Yogyakarta — and deep in chip-level work: FPGA boards, my own RISC-V SoC designs, and a photo diary of it all.

ppf.label: Future
ppf.title: Where I'm going
ppf.text: Master electronics engineering in chip design — then build my own business in electronics engineering.

present.title: Yogyakarta, semester by semester
present.text: Right now I'm a master's student at UGM — second semester in 2026 — spending my days between campus, the lab bench, and the mountains and beaches around Yogyakarta on weekends.

cards.title: Master's at UGM
cards.text: Campus life in Yogyakarta — lectures, coursework, and going deeper into electronics than my bachelor's ever allowed.

cards.title: Down to the chip level
cards.text: My current bench work is pure chip design territory: a Lattice ECP5 FPGA running PicoRV32, my own custom MRISCV SoC, a 7-segment chip decoder, SPI RAM, PCB layouts in Eagle, and even handmade inductors and crystal ladder filters.

cards.title: "Susanto" — my photo diary
cards.text: My Telegram channel is where this chapter gets documented as it happens — chip work, campus, travel, and everyday Yogyakarta life.

stats.label: Photos posted on my Telegram channel

future.headline: In the next few years: master electronics engineering in chip design — then build my own business in electronics engineering.
future.text: Every step so far points the same way. I started by programming microcontrollers; now I'm designing what goes inside them. The destination is deep chip-design mastery — and a company of my own built on it.

phases.title: Go deep on chip design
items: Finish my master's at UGM strong

phases.title: Become a chip designer

phases.title: Build my own business
items: Design products — and chips — of my own
Grow it from Yogyakarta / Surabaya to the world

rival.title: My rival: Jensen Huang
rival.text: Everyone needs a benchmark. Mine is the person who turned chips into the engine of modern computing. A one-sided rivalry — he doesn't know I exist yet — but it keeps my bar high.

them.label: The benchmark
them.name: Jensen Huang
points: Co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and has led it as CEO ever since
Built a company around GPUs, CUDA and AI computing
Proof that a chip company can change the whole world

me.label: The challenger
me.name: Abidul Qohar
points: Designing my own RISC-V SoC (MRISCV) and running PicoRV32 on a Lattice ECP5 FPGA
Moving from programming microcontrollers to designing the chips inside them
Goal: build my own electronics engineering business

rival.note: Rivals are how I measure how far I still have to go. The plan is simple: learn chip design deeply, build real products, and keep shipping.
